text:
B: Hiya! Can you hear me alright?
A: Yes, I can hear you. I am Tomasz. I'm in Reading.
B: I'm Hannah, Norwich. Nice to meet you. How did you find the puzzle thing at the start?
A: It was fine. I finished with about one minute left.
B: Oh, show-off! I ran out of time completely. So what do you do, Tomasz?
A: I am a student. Construction Management at University of Reading, second year. Before that I worked six years at a distribution warehouse near Theale, shift team leader. I still do some weekend shifts there in summer.
B: Oh, that's brilliant. Did you go back to study later on, then? Sorry, that sounds rude.
A: No, it's fine. I started at thirty-one. So yes, later than most.
B: I'm the same, sort of. I'm doing an Open University degree part-time, Arts and Humanities. I left uni at nineteen and I've always felt a bit, I don't know, unfinished about it. So I really admire anyone going back.
A: Mm. It is a lot of work, to be honest. But I keep a spreadsheet of every deadline, so it's manageable.
B: A spreadsheet! I saw your wall planner in the photo, with all the highlighter. I thought, he's organised.
A: Yes. Different colour for each module. Red is group project.
B: Why red?
A: Because the group project is a problem. One person has not done his part of site report. Deadline is next week.
B: Oh no. That's like my job, honestly. I run the lunchtime team at a primary school, six supervisors, so I do the rota and someone's always ringing in sick on chips Friday.
A: You do the rota? Then you understand. At the warehouse I did the rota for forty people. If someone doesn't come, you have to know who can cover, straight away.
B: Exactly! Do you do it on paper or...?
A: Excel. Always Excel.
B: I've got a whiteboard and a lot of hope. So what do you want to do after, once you've finished?
A: Site manager or assistant project manager. Graduate scheme with a contractor in Thames Valley. Then chartered with CIOB, and buy a house, Woodley or Wokingham.
B: That's really clear. I'm hoping for museum learning, like running workshops for school groups at Norwich Castle. I love old buildings, actually, medieval churches especially, I sketch them. You probably look at buildings in a totally different way, though. Like, is it going to fall down?
A: Sort of, yes. I look at how it's built, what is the load, how much it costs. Not if it is beautiful.
B: Ha, fair. Do you ever go and see things, like galleries or anything, or is that not really your thing?
A: Not really, no. To be honest I don't see much point. I watch engineering videos on YouTube. That is my gallery.
B: That's a good line, I might steal that. Have you got family over here, or are they back in Poland? I'm guessing Poland, sorry.
A: Yes, Poland. Rzeszów. My wife is here with me, she's a dental nurse in Wokingham. My parents are in Poland. We go twice a year, Christmas and summer.
B: Do you miss it?
A: Sometimes. My father is not very well, so. It's difficult being far.
B: Oh, I'm sorry. That must be hard. I lost my dad a few years ago, so I...
A: I'm sorry.
B: Thanks. It was a while back now. Anyway, what do you do to switch off, when you're not studying?
A: I run. Three mornings, 5k round Maiden Erlegh Lake. This week I was thirty seconds slower because of rain.
B: Thirty seconds slower and you're annoyed about it? My parkrun time hasn't improved in about two years, I just sort of...
